national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today held talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the 26th annual Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in the capital city of Kyrgyzstan, Bishkek. The discussions focused on key areas of India-Russia bilateral cooperation, including trade and investment, energy and defence. During the meeting, Prime Minister Modi said it was a matter of deep satisfaction that cooperation between India and Russia continued to scale new heights. On the Ukraine conflict, PM Modi stressed the need for a peaceful resolution, saying that every day of war sets humanity back. He told President Putin that resolving all issues through peaceful means is a call of humanity. PM Modi said, ” We must move from endless wars to ending wars,’ adding that India supports all efforts towards peace. The meeting took place more than a week before President Putin is scheduled to travel to India to attend the annual BRICS summit. During the meeting, the Prime Minister said India is hosting the BRICS Summit in a few days, and all Indians are eager to welcome Mr Putin and his delegation. He said the visit of the Russian President will strengthen bilateral relations and further reinforce dialogue and cooperation within the BRICS framework. President Vladimir Putin showed his satisfaction that Indian-Russian relations continue to strengthen on the basis of the principles of a special and privileged partnership.

national_raw_news.title: Sensex and Nifty close 0.4% down today 11 hours ago 149
national_raw_news.content: Benchmark domestic equity indices ended 0.4% down today. The Sensex declined 307 points to close at 76,957. The Nifty dropped 95 points to settle at 24,800. Meanwhile, the broader market at the National Stock Exchange displayed a mixed trend. The Midcap 100 index gained 0.2%, while the Smallcap 100 index dipped 0.7 per cent. Earlier, the markets opened on a weak note as escalating geopolitical tensions in West Asia and rising crude oil prices weighed on investor sentiment. Both the indices witnessed selling pressure across most sectors throughout the session. In the Sensex pack, 20 out of 30 companies registered losses. Among the top underperformers, Adani Ports declined 4.1%, ITC dropped around 3.7%, and Bharti Airtel lost nearly 2.8%. In contrast, Sun Pharma gained 1.9%, ICICI Bank added 1.7%, and Axis Bank rose one and a half per cent. In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 21 out of 28 sectors edged downward. Among the top laggards, Utilities decreased 2.6%, Metal lost 2.4%, and Services dipped 1.9%. In contrast, MidSmall Private Banks Quality Tilt rose over 1.2%, MidSmall Private Banks gained 1.2%, and Bankex added over 0.3%. The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 2572 companies declined, 1858 advanced and 250 remained unchanged.
